question: A unilateral nasal polyp in an adult is a red-flag finding that should prompt urgent investigation to exclude malignancy or inverted papilloma.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Benign nasal polyps are characteristically bilateral. Any unilateral polypoid nasal mass is a red flag demanding CT imaging and biopsy to rule out malignancy or inverted papilloma.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. True nasal polyps are almost always bilateral. A unilateral nasal mass — even if it looks polypoid — must be biopsied and imaged to exclude inverted papilloma (pre-malignant), squamous cell carcinoma, or other sinonasal neoplasm.
